case_name: Lalit Bhola vs Nidhi Bhola & Anr.
facts_of_case: The parties got married in 2007. A child was born out of wedlock in 2008. The wife filed an application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. seeking maintenance from the husband. The trial court granted interim maintenance, which was later reduced.

legal_principles.principle: Courts are not only guided by the income of the husband in determining the amount of monthly maintenance.
legal_principles.held: While awarding maintenance under Section 125 Cr.P.C. or maintenance pendente lite under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act or the maintenance under Section 18 of the Hindu Adoption or Maintenance Act, Courts are not only guided by the income of the husband in determining the amount of monthly maintenance.
cited_cases: Alok Kumar Jain v. Purnima Jain, (2007) DRJ 115

legal_principles.principle: Several factors including the status of the parties, liabilities, if any, of the husband and number of persons to be maintained by the husband would be some of the factors to be taken into consideration.
legal_principles.held: The Higher Courts have held that several factors including the status of the parties, liabilities, if any, of the husband and number of persons to be maintained by the husband would be some of the factors to be taken into consideration.
cited_cases: Alok Kumar Jain v. Purnima Jain, (2007) DRJ 115
Lalit Bhola vs Nidhi Bhola & Anr., (2013) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: The amount required by the wife to live a similar life style as she enjoyed in the matrimonial home keeping in view food, clothing, shelter, educational and medical needs of the wife and the children, if any, residing with the wife and payment capacity of the husband.
legal_principles.held: The amount required by the wife to live a similar life style as she enjoyed in the matrimonial home keeping in view food, clothing, shelter, educational and medical needs of the wife and the children, if any, residing with the wife and payment capacity of the husband.
cited_cases: Lalit Bhola vs Nidhi Bhola & Anr., (2013) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: There cannot be any mathematical formula for award of the maintenance amount such as 1/3rd or any other proportion of the husband's income.
legal_principles.held: It was held that there cannot be any mathematical formula for award of the maintenance amount such as 1/3rd or any other proportion of the husband's income.
cited_cases: Dev Dutt Singh v. Smt. Rajni Gandhi, AIR 1984 Del 320

outcome.final_order: The overall maintenance of `12,500/- is excessive and arbitrary.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for reduction of maintenance order
advising on interim maintenance in divorce cases
representing a client seeking modification of maintenance order
